title: Reduce storage and host-class uncertainty before implementation
description:
## Purpose

Buy down the uncertainty in `chatticus-fbae4e` by trying things for real, before any implementation is authorized.

This epic is **experiments and cheap fact-checks only**. Nothing here builds product code. Each child states the question it answers, what would falsify the current design, and what it costs to run.

## Why this ordering

Working out what each unknown actually gates produced a result worth recording, because it is not the order the initiative's own narrative suggests:

| Piece of the design | Needs tunnel? | Needs WAN NFS? | Value | Gated by an experiment here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EFS for AWS hosts (delete lease, snapshot, hydrate) | No | No | High — large deletion | **None.** No unknowns block it. |
| Accelerated batch (GPU on owned hardware) | No | No | Highest — $100s–$1000s per run | Long-running job spike |
| Local *interactive* host (Antharchy GUI) | Yes | Yes | Lowest — ~$30–60/mo | NFS-over-WAN spike |

**The WAN metadata question — flagged in the initiative as "load-bearing and unmeasured" — gates only the least valuable piece.** The EFS simplification for AWS hosts has no WAN dependency, and accelerated batch needs neither EFS nor a tunnel. That makes the NFS spike safe to defer and the long-running-job spike the one to run first.

## Ordering

1. **Long-running job spike** — gates the highest-value host class, independent of everything else.
2. **Cheap fact-checks** (Fargate capabilities, turn concurrency) — minutes each, no spike required.
3. **NFS-over-WAN spike** — run before committing engineering time to the local interactive host, not before the two tracks that do not depend on it.

## Not experiments

Recorded here so nobody spends a spike on them: AWS pricing (look it up), and reverse SSH tunnelling from behind home NAT (thoroughly established; latency is worth knowing eventually but would not change the design).
